review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people argue that advertisement brings some benefits for economic, many others hold a different opinion, saying that advertising made people dissatisfied with their life. I believe that there are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, one might argue that advertising has given rise to several benefits for undeniable economic. Chief among them is creating content and appealing visual effects employed on each platform where they are shown. This tendency is further reinforced by consumers, who spend money on this and help increasing spend power, and encouraged consumers buy this production. So creating more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation, which boost the economy. For example, some e-commerce platforms such as Shopee and Lazada in Vietnam, rely heavily on advertisement campaigns to attract their customers, and boosting not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector. Addition, advertising also create creative some jobs in marketing, media and design, which make it an important driver of economic activity.

On the other hand, one might believe that advertising made people have frustration in their lives with what they own, and advert has negative social consequences. On social media, it constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards or luxury possessions which emerge among viewers in foster dissatisfaction. For instance, in particular, young people feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadget by advertised on Tiktok or Facebook, which lead to frustration when they cannot afford them. Finally, leading to a society promoted materialistic values and money in the long run.
In my opinion, both views, valid to some certain extent that advertising may contributed to social dissatisfaction, by it's also play a crucial role in economic development.

review.overall: Em đã hoàn thành đủ bốn đoạn, có hai view, ví dụ Shopee/Lazada và ý social dissatisfaction. Tuy nhiên, bài còn ẩu ở lỗi nền tảng và nhiều câu không có cấu trúc hoàn chỉnh, đặc biệt ở Body 1, cuối Body 2 và Conclusion. Em cần viết lại bài này, tự soát từng động từ và từng mắt xích trước khi nộp.

paragraphs: Some people argue that advertising brings economic benefits, whereas others believe that it can make people dissatisfied with their lives. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand. This encourages people to spend more, which increases production and creates employment opportunities and state revenue through taxation. E-commerce platforms such as Shopee and Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting their sales and the digital retail sector. Furthermore, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media and design, making it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Advertisements on social media constantly show perfect lifestyles, beauty standards and luxury possessions, which can foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook. This pressure can lead to frustration when they cannot afford these items and may promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run.
In conclusion, both views are valid to some extent. Advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction, while also playing a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: There is an argument that students with the best academic results deserve rewards, while others say that students who make progress should also receive rewards. I strongly believe that both groups of students should receive praise.

Admittedly, high-achieving students deserve recognition for their results. Initially, these students have diligently applied themselves to their studies. They deserve their praises and privileges. This may also encourage these students and others to study harder to win the reward. Such motivation may raise academic performance more broadly. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students can become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, schools should reward not only high-achieving students but also those who make progress in their studies. To begin with, if only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, others may think that their effort is futile. This is because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, rewarding progress can encourage all students to be diligent and help them understand that they need to keep improving themselves. They can do so irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit them more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students with the highest results and students who have made progress.

Some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an argument that parents, in some areas, should choose to teach their children at home, which brings more benefits than giving them to school. Personally, I am not firmly of the same school.

Someone says that homeschooling is good for both parent and their children when choose this way. Initially, this allows parents to save money, without school fees are required. At home, children is educated by this way they are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure and cause emotional or mental problems. Additionally, when parents teaching their children at home by themselves is tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, which are often not seen the case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, almost things are be seen as advantages that are among the main chief of drawbacks. This can bee seen the way in this education approach is not actually save money, which even is needed to pay a larger amount of money for lab equipment and tutors, and entails that one parent need to be cut off, lead to, cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Furthermore, most parents are not well, or actually don't have enough knowledge or versed in all school subjects, which can be due to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. Finally, social problems that children are faced with at school such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, which also prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I am not firmly convinced that homeschooling is a good choice for parents, which entails more disadvantages than benefits.

paragraphs: There is an argument that parents in some areas should choose to teach their children at home rather than send them to school. Personally, I do not share this view: the disadvantages of homeschooling are greater than its benefits.

Supporters say that homeschooling is good for both parents and their children. Initially, it allows parents to save money as no school fees are required. In addition, children educated at home are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which can cause emotional or mental problems. Additionally, when parents teach their children at home themselves, they can tailor the curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, which is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to large classes.

However, these apparent advantages have substantial drawbacks. Initially, this approach may not actually save money, as parents need to pay more for lab equipment and tutors, and one parent may need to set aside working time to cater for the child's academic or personal needs. Furthermore, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, which can make it difficult to explain concepts properly and may cause academic problems. Finally, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I am convinced that homeschooling brings more disadvantages than benefits and is generally not the best choice for parents.
